elements.element: Customer has a right to terminate for convenience
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience"

elements.element: Notice period of 30 days, in writing
elements.evidence: "upon 30 days' prior written notice to Vendor"

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on such termination
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term."
"upon 30 days' prior written notice" (shorter than 60–90 days; preferred bargain instead)

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee appears; clause provides only "Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees"

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at end of a term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate ... for convenience during a committed term" (no end-of-term 90-day right granted)

reasons: The inserted 9.4 completes all four atomic elements of the preferred position: Customer convenience right, 30 days' written notice, refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (pro-rata in effect), and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a committed term.

Fallback is not satisfied on its own terms (30-day notice, no early-termination fee, no end-of-term Vendor right), which is immaterial because the locked target is preferred and the levels are separate bargains.
Minimal: a single concise insertion into Section 9 where no convenience-termination clause existed; no rewrite of Sections 9.1–9.5, no new exceptions, no boilerplate, no borrowed fallback mechanics.

Untouched terms (breach, insolvency, cause-based Order Form termination, non-exclusivity of remedies, Section 8.1 term/survival of Order Forms) remain fully effective; no undefined term is introduced (Fees, Order Form, Vendor are defined).

Residual point to note in the rationale, not a deviation: Section 2.1's take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" sits in tension with the new right, so consider confirming whether termination under 9.4 relieves the remaining committed spend.
